checkpoints: Redis presence tracking that stores a single online/offline bit per user only works correctly when each user has exactly one connection at a time; the moment a user has multiple simultaneous connections (phone and laptop, or two browser tabs), the single bit can no longer represent their true state.

A user's real online status is the union of every connection they currently have open, not a reflection of whichever connection most recently changed state — so a disconnect on one device should only affect the shared bit if it was that user's last remaining connection.

Calling `SETBIT presence:online <userId> 0` unconditionally inside `disconnect()` means the very FIRST disconnect for a user clears the bit, even while other connections for that same user are still alive on other nodes — the correct behavior is for only the LAST disconnect to clear it.

The missing piece is a per-user reference count: without tracking how many live connections a user currently has, `connect()` and `disconnect()` have no way to distinguish 'this was one of several connections' from 'this was the only connection.'

The fix is a per-user connection counter stored in Redis (e.g. `presence:conn:<userId>`), incremented with `INCR` on every `connect()` and decremented with `DECR` on every `disconnect()`, so the counter reflects the total number of live connections across the whole cluster.

The online bit should only be written on the edges of that counter: `SETBIT ... 1` fires solely on the 0-to-1 transition (the first connection appearing), and `SETBIT ... 0` (plus removing the counter key) fires solely on the 1-to-0 transition (the last connection disappearing) — connects and disconnects in between just adjust the count without touching the bit.

The counter must live in shared Redis rather than in either node's local process memory, because a user's connections can land on different nodes behind a load balancer; each node only sees its own in-memory state, so only a value that every node can atomically read and update turns 'does this user have any connection left anywhere in the cluster?' into one race-free, globally consistent answer.

Correctness of the fix can be verified by opening two connections for the same user on two different nodes and confirming the online count stays at 1, closing one connection and confirming the user still shows online, and only seeing the state flip to offline once the very last connection closes.
